title: What is the HCF of fourteen times six and fourteen times nine?
description: Fourteen times six and fourteen times nine are written as products of primes. Fourteen is a common factor, but the numbers also share a three, so the highest common factor is fourteen times three. Keeko doubts this and thinks fourteen is already the highest.
teaching_notes: One idea: two multiples of the same number share that number, and also whatever the other two numbers share. Watch for students who stop at the common multiplier and miss a further shared prime.

video_script.why: The child can find a highest common factor from the primes and now meets two numbers that are multiples of the same number.
video_script.substitution: Write both numbers as products of primes, look for the shared primes, and multiply them.
video_script.anchor: The two products 14 × 6 and 14 × 9 written one under the other, with the prime products beside them.
video_script.wrong_answer: so the highest common factor is fourteen
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees fourteen in both numbers and stops there, but six and nine still share a three, so the highest common factor is fourteen times three.
video_script.payoff_line: The highest common factor is forty two
never_show: 14 as the highest common factor, marked right
maths_rules: shared primes: one 2, one 7 and one 3; 2 × 7 = 14 and the extra shared 3
video_script.design: One idea: besides the common multiplier, look for what the other two numbers share. The two products stay on the board from step one to the answer.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko sees fourteen in both numbers, so the highest common factor is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Fourteen is a common factor, but is it the highest? Six and nine still share a three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Fourteen does not hold that three, so there is more to find. The answer stays forty two.
